oneLiner: AMD is the market's chosen second source for AI compute - record Q2 2026 results and gigawatt-scale OpenAI/Meta/Anthropic commitments now demand flawless Helios/MI450 execution at a multiple that already assumes it.
thesis: Data center is compounding at triple-digit rates. Q2 2026 data center revenue of $6.7B grew 107% YoY on EPYC share gains and the Instinct MI400-series ramp, and is now 58% of total revenue.

The customer roster de-risks the roadmap. OpenAI (6GW, first 1GW of MI450 beginning H2 2026), Meta (6GW expanded deal, Feb 2026) and Anthropic (up to 2GW of MI450 in Helios, first GW in 1H 2027) represent multi-year committed demand.

Helios closes the rack-scale gap with Nvidia. AMD's first rack-scale system (Venice CPUs + MI450 GPUs + networking + software) is in production, with second-generation MI455X Helios shipments to Meta and OpenAI beginning in the coming months.
Margins are holding through the GPU ramp. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 56% in Q2 (+200bps+ YoY) and is guided at ~56% for Q3, undercutting the bear case that AI GPU mix must dilute margins.
Client is a quiet share-gain story. Client revenue rose 23% YoY to $3.1B on record mobile processor sales, continuing share capture from Intel.

latestProse: Q2 2026 (reported Aug 4): revenue $11.5B, +50% YoY and a record, with non-GAAP gross margin of 56% (+200bps+ YoY), non-GAAP EPS $1.66 (GAAP $1.38). Data center drove everything: $6.7B, +107% YoY, 58% of sales, on EPYC and Instinct. Client rose 23% to $3.1B on record mobile sales; gaming fell 31% to $779M on late-cycle semi-custom. The disclosure that matters most: Helios, AMD's first rack-scale platform, is in production, and second-gen Helios with MI455X begins shipping to Meta and OpenAI in the coming months - the proof point that AMD can sell systems, not just chips. The stock still fell ~7% after hours.
guidanceProse: Q3 2026 guidance is revenue of ~$13.0B plus or minus $300M (about +41% YoY) with non-GAAP gross margin of approximately 56% - a beat-and-raise on revenue but a margin guide that did not move, which is the entire post-print debate. Bulls read flat 56% through an accelerating GPU mix as evidence rack-scale AI is margin-neutral at worst; bears note record results plus GW-scale deal announcements produced zero margin leverage, hinting AMD is pricing (and issuing warrants) to buy share. Management says data center AI grows well over 100% with momentum into 2027 as OpenAI's first gigawatt deploys in H2 2026.

guide.label: Q3 2026 revenue guide
guide.sub: ~+41% YoY at midpoint; non-GAAP gross margin ~56%

segments: Data center: $6.7B, 58% of revenue, +107% YoY (EPYC CPUs + Instinct GPUs)
Client: $3.1B, ~27% of revenue, +23% YoY; Gaming: $779M, ~7%, -31% YoY
competitive: Nvidia holds ~75-80% of AI accelerator revenue in 2026; AMD is a ~6-7% share second source - the bull case is that share roughly doubling
Blackwell/B300 sold out into mid-2026 made AMD capacity strategically valuable to capacity-starved hyperscalers
Hyperscaler custom silicon (Google TPU, AWS Trainium, Broadcom ASICs) is a larger, faster-growing threat to merchant GPU vendors than AMD is to Nvidia
Versus Intel: continued client/server x86 share gains, though 18A-based Panther Lake and Clearwater Forest are Intel's first credible response in years
Cerebras partnership (Jul 23, 2026) pairs Helios throughput with wafer-scale low-latency decode - up to 5x tokens/sec/watt - a differentiated inference answer to Nvidia
moat: AMD's moat is chiplet design execution plus the only complete CPU+GPU+networking rack-scale alternative to Nvidia, reinforced by customers who strategically need a second source. ROCm software remains the soft flank versus CUDA, and the warrant-laced OpenAI structure shows AMD still pays for demand certainty rather than commanding it.
risks: Priced for perfection. ~63x forward earnings versus Nvidia at ~23x; the stock fell ~7% on a beat-and-raise simply because the margin guide was flat.
Warrant dilution. Up to 160M shares (roughly 10% of the base) issuable to OpenAI as milestones vest, with the first tranche tied to the 1GW deployment starting H2 2026.
Rack-scale execution risk. Helios is AMD's first rack-scale system; slips in MI450/MI455X, cooling or networking would cascade into 2027 committed deployments.
Consumer weakness. Gaming fell 31% YoY and management concedes pricing is weighing on consumer demand.
Customer concentration in a circular AI capex cycle. Demand concentrates in a few AI labs and hyperscalers whose financing - OpenAI's especially - is aggressive and unproven.
Nvidia's next generation plus custom ASICs could compress the share-gain window before AMD banks the earnings.
catalysts: H2 2026: first 1GW OpenAI MI450 deployment begins (first warrant tranche vests)
H2 2026: AMD-Cerebras joint inference solution available via Cerebras Cloud
1H 2027: first gigawatt of Anthropic Helios deployment begins
pricedIn: Shares trade around $485 after the ~7% post-earnings pullback (mid-Aug 2026), with consensus forward P/E of roughly 63-64x - far above AMD's own pre-AI-ramp range and roughly triple Nvidia's ~23x. The price already assumes the gigawatt agreements convert to revenue on schedule, gross margin holds ~56%, and data center AI more than doubles again. The key debate: are GW-scale deals effectively a contracted backlog justifying the premium, or is AMD buying share with pricing and 160M warrant shares, meaning EPS never catches up to the multiple?

scenarios.bear: MI450/Helios ramp slips or margins finally dilute as GPU mix rises; OpenAI-linked demand proves financing-constrained. Estimates flatten, and a 60x+ multiple compresses toward peer levels - the stock roughly halves even with revenue still growing.
scenarios.base: Q3's ~$13B lands, OpenAI's first gigawatt deploys in H2 2026, data center AI grows well over 100% into 2027 with margins pinned near 56%. The stock grinds higher with estimate revisions while the multiple gradually compresses as EPS catches up.
scenarios.bull: Helios becomes the default second-source rack, AMD's accelerator share climbs from ~6-7% toward low-teens of a $200B+ market, and Meta/Anthropic/OpenAI deployments stack in 2027 alongside the MI500 launch. Estimates step-change upward.

valPresets.note: At ~63x forward, even the bear preset needs 15% year-1 FCF growth - the reverse DCF quantifies how much of the gigawatt pipeline is already in the price.
